subject: Qualification: PoC trial plan & deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated) — ACME Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery — Deployment mode needs / PoC next steps

Alex/Priya — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed PoC plan attached.

Summary of what I heard from your side:
- Primary goal: validate inference latency and throughput for customer-facing recommendation API (real-time scoring).
- Preferred deployment: leaning toward Dedicated capacity due to predictable throughput and isolation, but you have a couple of security/data-residency items to confirm before signing up.
- Success criteria we agreed on: p95 latency < 200ms at 1k QPS burst (steady-state 500 req/s), model output parity vs current baseline (within 2% for key quality metrics), end-to-end telemetry (request tracing + audit logs).
- Timeline: you’d like a 2-week hands-on trial/PoC starting mid-May.

Attached: provisional PoC trial plan (poc-trial-plan-acme-20270426.pdf) and our security checklist (security-checklist-acme-20270426.xlsx). The plan covers two paths depending on whether you proceed with Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity:
- Hosted API path (fastest): we provision a dedicated tenant with rate limits and data isolation controls; good for speed-to-test but has shared control plane.
- Dedicated capacity path: reserved GPU pool for ACME with pinned throughput & private networking options (VPC peering). Requires some networking prep from your infra team but provides stronger performance guarantees.

Proposed next steps (please confirm):
1) Confirm preferred path (Hosted vs Dedicated) by EOD Wed 2027-04-28 so we can lock resources.
2) If Dedicated, please share contact for your networking lead (name + email) to coordinate VPC peering and firewall rules.
3) We (Marissa) will kick off the onboarding checklist and provision trial capacity once we have the stakeholders.
4) We’ll schedule a 30m kickoff (technical) the week of May 10 to walk through traffic replay, monitoring, and success metric collection.

If you prefer, we can start with Hosted for the first week while Dedicated is being stood up — that’s a common approach to reduce time-to-first-test.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once I hear which path you prefer.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0134

---
Attachment: poc-trial-plan-acme-20270426.pdf (PDF, 8 pages)
Attachment: security-checklist-acme-20270426.xlsx (XLSX, 12 rows)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery — Deployment mode needs / PoC next steps

Ben — thanks for the recap and the docs. Quick responses from our side: we are leaning toward Dedicated capacity for the PoC given our traffic profile and the need for consistent p95 latency during business hours. A few clarifications before we lock the path: 

1) Data residency: ACME needs logs and any persisted telemetry stored in our AWS account (us-east-1) or at minimum guaranteed encryption-at-rest with dedicated KMS keys. Is VPC + KMS integration available during the trial?
2) Network setup: we have a networking lead (Priya Reddy) and a security lead (Samir Patel). Priya (cc’d on this thread) will coordinate firewall rules and peering windows.
3) Cost/credits: can you confirm what the trial includes (GPU-hours, request quota) and an estimated committed cost if we convert to Dedicated for 3 months? We need an order-of-magnitude to route to procurement.

We can confirm the PoC start week of May 10 — Prefer May 10–21 (2 weeks). If you can stand up Hosted while Dedicated is provisioned, that’d be helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director, API Products | ACME Corp
alex.johnson@acme-corp.com
+1 (617) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme-corp.com>, Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Discovery — Deployment mode needs / PoC next steps

Alex/Priya — great, appreciate the quick clarity. Confirming actions and owners: 

- Deployment path: Dedicated capacity (confirmed). We’ll plan to provision a dedicated GPU pool in us-east-1 and enable VPC peering + KMS integration for telemetry persistence.
- Networking contact: Priya, please share the preferred contact window for VPC peering/testing and any /32 IP ranges we should expect from your side.
- Security items: Marissa will own the SOC2/audit evidence requests and coordinate the security checklist. Marissa — can you review the attached checklist and confirm which items we can satisfy during the trial vs require production controls?
- Trial scope & credits: Jordan — can you provision the following for the PoC and confirm available credits?
  - 2 x A100 equivalent GPUs (reserved for ACME)
  - 500 req/s sustained traffic profile with short bursts to 1k QPS for 15s windows
  - 2-week trial window (May 10–21)
  - Monitoring: token-level cost, p95 latency dashboards, and request tracing enabled

Deliverables and timeline: 
- Tue May 4: Networking kickoff between Priya + Jordan to exchange peering details and firewall rules.
- Mon May 10: PoC kickoff — traffic replay & baseline run (Hosted proxy available same day if needed).
- Fri May 21: End of trial, data & logs shared, evaluation call w/ ACME and Redwood (30–45m).

Decision criteria reminder (will be measured during trial):
- p95 latency < 200ms for 95% of test windows
- Quality parity: model outputs within agreed thresholds vs baseline
- Observability: full request traces and audit logs delivered to ACME S3 with KMS encryption

Next steps: Priya to confirm peering contact and timing; Marissa to review checklist; Jordan to confirm capacity and credits. I’ll set up the calendar invites once we have confirmation.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
